name: @tocharianou/lambda-tool-mcp

tools.name: list_functions
tools.description: List AWS Lambda functions in a region with runtime, handler, VPC config, state, and last-modified date. Supports prefix filtering to narrow results. Ideal for: discovering all Lambda functions in an account, identifying functions with VPC access (potential lateral movement paths), finding recently modified functions after a suspected compromise.

region.description: AWS region to list functions from (e.g. us-east-1). Defaults to AWS_DEFAULT_REGION.

functionPrefix.description: Optional prefix filter. Only functions whose names start with this prefix are returned. Example: "prod-" returns only prod-* functions.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of functions to return (1–200, default: 50).

break_token_rule.description: Set to true to bypass token limits in critical situations (default: false).

tools.name: get_function_details
tools.description: Get comprehensive Lambda function configuration: runtime, handler, IAM role, memory, timeout, environment variable KEYS (values redacted for security), VPC config, layers, tags, and code download URL. Flags potentially sensitive environment variable keys (SECRET, TOKEN, KEY, etc.). Ideal for: identifying hardcoded credential patterns, checking unexpected layer additions (supply chain attack), verifying the execution role for privilege escalation analysis.

functionName.description: Lambda function name or ARN. Example: "my-function" or "arn:aws:lambda:us-east-1:123456789012:function:my-function".

region.description: AWS region where the function is deployed. Defaults to AWS_DEFAULT_REGION.

break_token_rule.description: Set to true to bypass token limits in critical situations (default: false).

tools.name: get_function_policy
tools.description: Get the resource-based (IAM) policy of a Lambda function showing who can invoke it. Highlights public principals ("*"), cross-account access, and AWS service principals. Ideal for: detecting publicly accessible functions (AuthType NONE backdoors), identifying unexpected cross-account invocation grants, auditing service-triggered functions (API Gateway, S3, SNS triggers).

functionName.description: Lambda function name or ARN to inspect the resource-based policy for.

break_token_rule.description: Set to true to bypass token limits in critical situations (default: false).

tools.name: list_event_source_mappings
tools.description: List event source mappings (SQS, DynamoDB Streams, Kinesis, Kafka) that trigger Lambda functions. Flags DynamoDB stream triggers as potential data exfiltration paths. Ideal for: detecting persistence mechanisms planted by attackers (malicious SQS/SNS triggers that re-invoke a backdoor), mapping data pipelines that could be abused for exfiltration, auditing all automated invocation paths for a function.

functionName.description: Filter by function name or ARN. If omitted, returns event source mappings for all functions in the region.

break_token_rule.description: Set to true to bypass token limits in critical situations (default: false).

tools.name: get_function_url_config
tools.description: Check if a Lambda function has a public Function URL (HTTPS endpoint) and inspect its auth type and CORS. Flags AuthType=NONE (publicly invocable without credentials) and wildcard CORS origins. Ideal for: discovering public-facing serverless backdoors, identifying unauthenticated function endpoints planted by attackers, auditing CORS misconfigurations that enable cross-origin data exfiltration.

functionName.description: Lambda function name or ARN to check for a public Function URL.

break_token_rule.description: Set to true to bypass token limits in critical situations (default: false).
